findings.problem: The hint rules out caminar but not pasear, which is a common and correct answer for walking around a place on foot, especially for pleasure.
findings.fix: hint: to go about on foot, not caminar or pasear

findings.problem: The example uses andar as an infinitive after gusta rather than a conjugated form of andar.
findings.fix: example.es: Ando por el parque todas las mañanas. / example.en: I walk around the park every morning.

back.es: to walk, to go around (on foot); also to be (going around), to be up to
back.example: Me gusta andar por el parque. = I like walking around the park.

note: The irregular flag is right because of the preterite anduve, even though the present tense is regular; in most of Latin America caminar is the everyday word for walking, so this sense of andar is less central than the "to be (going around)" card.
